evidence: Liv. 1.4.6: ad puerīlem vāgītum cursum flexisse
terms.comment: In the direction of a thing, whether one gets there or not (see to).

terms.grammar: adverb placed after its noun: after ad or in + accusative, or after the accusative alone of a town’s name
evidence: Sulp. in Cic. Fam. 4.5.4: ab Aegīnā Megaram versus nāvigārem
Cic. Lael. 96: in forum versus agere cum populō
terms.comment: It marks the direction only: Megaram versus, towards Megara; in forum versus, facing the forum; ad Ōceanum versus, towards the Ocean (Caes.).

terms.grammar: adverb, with a dative and a verb of motion
evidence: Cic. Fam. 14.5.1: quam longissimē poteris obviam nōbīs prōdeās
terms.comment: Going towards someone who is coming: obviam īre, prōdīre, venīre, go out to meet.

phrases.latin: ad tē reptantī, puer īnsidiōse, lacertae parce
phrases.english: spare the lizard creeping towards you, sly boy

phrases.latin: lupam sitientem ex montibus quī circā sunt ad puerīlem vāgītum cursum flexisse
phrases.english: that a thirsty she-wolf from the hills round about turned her steps towards the children’s crying

phrases.latin: ex Asiā rediēns cum ab Aegīnā Megaram versus nāvigārem
phrases.english: on my way back from Asia, as I was sailing from Aegina towards Megara

phrases.latin: quam longissimē poteris obviam nōbīs prōdeās
phrases.english: come out to meet us as far along the road as you can

phrases.latin: Currēns itaque Esau obviam frātrī suō, amplexātus est eum
phrases.english: so Esau ran to meet his brother and embraced him
